{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{Redirect|EA EA|other topics|EAEA (disambiguation){{!}}EAEA}}
{{more footnotes|date=April 2013}}
'''Craige Schensted''' ({{Daterangedash|1927-04-12|2021-01-22|mdy}}),<ref name="obituary">{{Cite web |title=Obituary of Ea Ea|url=https://ripostafh.com/tribute/details/16196/Ea-Ea/obituary.html |access-date=1 June 2025 |website=Riposta Funeral Home}}</ref> who formally changed his name to '''Ea Ea''', was an American physicist and mathematician who first formulated the insertion algorithm {{harv|Schensted|1961}} that defines the [[Robinson–Schensted correspondence]]. Under a different form, that correspondence had earlier been described by [[Gilbert de Beauregard Robinson]] in 1938, but it is due to the Schensted insertion algorithm that the correspondence has become widely known in [[combinatorics]]. Schensted also designed several board games including [[*Star]],  [[Star (board game)|Star]], and [[Y (game)|Y]].

In 1995, he changed his name to  '''Ea''', the Babylonian name for the Sumerian god [[Enki]], interested in the god's creative and empathetic nature.<ref name="obituary"/> This became '''Ea Ea''' in 1999, in anticipation of the [[Year 2000 problem|millennium computer glitches]]. He lived for forty years on [[Peaks Island, Maine|Peaks Island]] in [[Portland, Maine]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://gamepuzzles.com/ea-star.htm |title=Star Inventor: Ea Ea (Craige Schensted) |access-date=May 30, 2025}}</ref>
